edges.description: Falling cardiac output and effective arterial underfilling unload the arterial baroreceptors and reduce renal perfusion, which is the stimulus that switches on the sympathetic nervous system and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system in heart failure.

The failing ventricle cannot augment stroke volume and cardiac output to meet the metabolic demand of exertion, which is the proximate cause of the reduced exercise capacity that defines functional class.
Inadequate cardiac output limits oxygen delivery to skeletal muscle and other tissues at rest and on mild exertion, producing the persistent tiredness characteristic of the syndrome.
Angiotensin II and aldosterone are two of the inputs feeding the shared profibrotic effectors, which is why blockade upstream of the mineralocorticoid receptor does not silence the programme.

edges.description: Sustained sympathetic and RAAS signalling drives the maladaptive hypertrophic and fibrotic growth programme in the ventricle, converting an initially compensatory response into progressive structural remodelling.

Angiotensin II and aldosterone promote renal sodium and water reabsorption and arginine vasopressin promotes free-water retention, which is the neurohormonal route to volume overload in heart failure.

Hypertrophy, chamber dilatation and interstitial fibrosis increase diastolic stiffness and degrade systolic performance, so the structural response that was initially compensatory ends up worsening pump function. This closes the self-reinforcing loop that drives progression of the syndrome.
Volume overload raises left atrial and pulmonary venous pressure, driving fluid into the pulmonary interstitium and alveoli and producing the cardinal breathlessness of heart failure.

In the recumbent position the retained volume redistributes from the splanchnic and lower-body reservoirs to the thorax, raising pulmonary capillary pressure further and producing breathlessness on lying flat.
Systemic venous congestion from the expanded extracellular volume raises capillary hydrostatic pressure in dependent tissues, driving interstitial fluid accumulation.
Convergent profibrotic signalling drives cardiac fibroblast activation and interstitial extracellular matrix accumulation.

nodes.description: In HFpEF, myocardial fibrosis is driven not by haemodynamic load alone but by several endocrine axes that converge on a small set of shared intracellular effectors. TGF-beta-Smad signalling receives simultaneous input from angiotensin II, aldosterone, cortisol, leptin, FGF23 and thyroid deficiency; NADPH oxidase-derived oxidative stress amplifies TGF-beta, cross-links matrix via lysyl oxidase, and drives ligand-independent mineralocorticoid receptor activation; and the NO-cGMP-PKG axis, normally a brake on fibroblast activation, is suppressed by virtually every endocrine disturbance in the syndrome. Because several axes feed each convergence point, and because self-reinforcing feedback circuits regenerate the signal, blocking any single shared effector is rapidly bypassed. This node is the reason the entry treats HFpEF fibrosis as multi-axis rather than as the downstream of one pathway.

nodes.description: Spironolactone or eplerenone for additional neurohormonal blockade, and the non-steroidal agent finerenone. The mechanistic case for adding an MRA on top of an ACE inhibitor or ARB is that those drugs leave the terminal mineralocorticoid receptor programme intact by several independent routes: chymase-dependent, ACE-independent angiotensin II generation circumvents ACE inhibition; aldosterone escape restores MR activation during chronic AT1 blockade; and cortisol regenerated by 11beta-HSD1, together with reactive oxygen species, drives ligand-independent Rac1-mediated MR activation. MR antagonism is therefore not a redundant second hit on the same pathway but the only one of the three drug classes that reaches the terminal effector.

nodes.description: HFpEF disproportionately affects postmenopausal women, and the review's account of why is structural rather than additive. Oestrogen normally restrains three profibrotic axes at once — it reduces ACE expression and AT1 receptor density, enhances insulin sensitivity through GLUT4 and IRS-1 signalling, and maintains an anti-inflammatory adipokine profile — so its withdrawal disinhibits all three in concert, producing the concentric, microvascular-predominant female phenotype.

nodes.description: 11beta-HSD1 regenerates active cortisol from cortisone inside adipose tissue, liver, vasculature and myocardium, so glucocorticoid exposure at the tissue level can be raised without any change in adrenal secretion. Chronic glucocorticoid excess promotes cardiac fibroblast proliferation, myofibroblast transdifferentiation and collagen synthesis through the glucocorticoid receptor, potentiates TGF-beta signalling, and suppresses nitric oxide availability. In non-epithelial tissue cortisol also binds the mineralocorticoid receptor with affinity comparable to aldosterone, so glucocorticoid excess can engage RAAS-like profibrotic programmes directly.
